transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Start time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Alex Morgan (CTO, Equinox), Sara Lopez (Head of Security, Equinox), Jamal Reed (Cloud Engineer), Lena Park (DevOps)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery: Equinox wants private deployment inside their AWS VPC, need to understand networking options, region constraints, and compliance.

[00:00] Marcus Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Marcus, AE on the account, with Priya our solutions engineer. Quick intros?
[00:12] Alex Morgan: Alex here, CTO at Equinox, I'll kind of drive the integrational bits, Sara is our security lead, Jamal handles cloud infra, Lena does DevOps.
[00:20] Sara Lopez: hi all.
[00:32] Marcus Chen: Great. Goal for today is to surface networking constraints for a Private/VPC deployment, figure out where to put models (region/AZ), and identify blockers for a POC. Priya, want to add?
[00:40] Priya Patel: Yep. We'll cover connectivity patterns: VPC peering, PrivateLink/private endpoints, options for routing egress, and how KMS + audit logs work for Private. Also we'll touch on latency expectations for our smaller LLMs vs larger models.
[01:05] Jamal Reed: One thing up front, we have tight egress controls, everything has to go through our transit gateway and a set of static NAT IPs. We also prefer to avoid cross-account peering where possible.
[01:20] Marcus Chen: Understood. So two common patterns: 1) Redwood deploys a control plane in our managed region and we create VPC peering/peers for data plane, or 2) we provide a private endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) and keep traffic via ENIs into your VPC. Both have tradeoffs.
[01:45] Sara Lopez: Peering is fine but our compliance team prefers endpoints/PrivateLink because it gives clearer audit boundaries, also less blast radius.
[02:05] Priya Patel: Right \u2014 PrivateLink uses interface endpoints, so Redwood would publish a service name and you create an interface endpoint in your VPC. That means all model inference traffic stays inside AWS backbone, you can attach endpoint policies, and it's cross-account safe. Downside: there are per-endpoint costs and some throughput limits per ENI unless you scale across AZs.
[02:32] Lena Park: If we do PrivateLink, do we still need NAT or can it go through our TGW? Our current setup forces all egress through NAT instances for logging/Azure... I mean for extra inspection.
[02:50] Jamal Reed: We usually route to a TGW and then to a set of inspection appliances. Concern is: does Redwood need outbound access to our S3 or will it be purely inside the VPC?
[03:12] Priya Patel: For Private deployment, Redwood's serving nodes run in your VPC (private subnets) and typically we only need S3 access for model artifacts if you're using our model registry; you can host artifacts in your own S3 with a VPC endpoint. For runtime we don't need internet egress except for an optional control plane connection (can be backhauled via a minimal outbound to our control endpoint or disabled in fully air-gapped setups).
[03:45] Alex Morgan: Data residency \u2014 we need all logs and raw prompt/response payloads to remain in-region and not transit to other regions. Can you pin the region of model serving?
[04:00] Marcus Chen: Absolutely. We can pin model serving to a specific region and even to specific AZs if needed; we do recommend multi-AZ for reliability but we can scope the POC to a single region. For the control plane, we can run a customer-controlled control plane in your account, or use a private control plane hosted in a customer VPC depending on your compliance.
[04:20] Sara Lopez: KMS \u2014 how do keys get managed? We must use our customer-managed KMS keys for any encryption of data at rest.
[04:35] Priya Patel: We support using your AWS KMS keys. Redwood will store model caches and ephemeral KV in EBS/EFS encrypted with your CMKs. For HSM integrations, we can integrate with external HSMs but that's part of an enterprise package and usually requires a deeper security review.
[05:00] [short crosstalk] Jamal Reed: So what's the network footprint \u2014 IP ranges we need to allow?
[05:10] Marcus Chen: We'll provide a list of IP prefixes for any managed services and for control-plane endpoints. If you're running the entire stack in your account, the footprint is primarily the subnets we deploy into, and you control the SGs. For PrivateLink, you'll only need to allow the interface endpoints.
[05:30] Lena Park: Can you give examples of latency numbers? We have strict SLAs for trading desk alerts \u2014 100ms round-trip for short prompts is ideal.
[05:50] Priya Patel: For our smaller distilled models, in-region p99 is typically sub-150ms on a 16GB GPU instance with local KV caching, but large models will be higher. A lot depends on sequence length and batching. Dedicated GPU pools lower jitter.
[06:20] Alex Morgan: That sounds reasonable. Our main use case initially is embedding + short generation for summarization and alerts. So probably smaller model families.
[06:35] Marcus Chen: Good fit. Next \u2014 routing: if your VPC forces all egress via TGW and inspection, we can deploy in private subnets that have routing to TGW; Redwood workers will then flow through your normal inspection. PrivateLink bypasses this unless you force endpoint routing through TGW \u2014 depends on your architecture.
[07:05] Jamal Reed: We definitely want inspection. How does that affect performance?
[07:15] Priya Patel: There's some added latency with middleboxes. We recommend benchmarking with your inspection path turned on in the POC. Our POC plan includes a benchmark harness you can run from within your environment.
[07:40] [08:15] Sara Lopez: Audit logs \u2014 we need request-level audit logs for compliance (who called which model, request IDs, timestamps). Do you stream logs to our SIEM?
[08:25] Marcus Chen: Yes, we can forward audit logs to your CloudWatch or S3 via Kinesis/Firehose. For Private deployments, logs can be entirely in your account. We also produce structured request/response metadata for retention policies.
[08:45] Priya Patel: Note that for payload retention we can redact or not persist prompts depending on configuration. We have retention policies configurable per-namespace.
[09:05] Alex Morgan: Any known blockers with cross-account PrivateLink + TGW? Our infra folks once had routing issues where interface endpoints didn't follow TGW route tables as expected.
[09:30] Jamal Reed: yeah that was a pain. The interface endpoints create ENIs in subnets \u2014 we had to create specific route tables.
[09:40] Priya Patel: Agreed \u2014 it's a common ops wrinkle. For customers using TGW we recommend we jointly diagram the traffic flow during the POC. We also sometimes use a proxy instance in a shared services VPC to avoid complex per-AZ ENI scaling.
[10:05] Marcus Chen: On the topic of scaling: PrivateLink ENIs can be a limiting factor if you have very high concurrent connections; we recommend multi-AZ endpoints and, if needed, a dedicated Egress/NAT pair or using direct VPC-hosted workers.
[10:35] [12:00] Alex Morgan: Security review \u2014 Sara, anything else from compliance?
[12:08] Sara Lopez: We'll want SOC2 Type II reports, network diagrams, dataflow, list of third-party subprocessors, and proof of KMS CMK usage. Also SSO/SAML for admin UI and RBAC.
[12:30] Marcus Chen: We'll share SOC2 artifacts (redacted) and a security pack. We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC, and audit hooks. I'll attach the security pack link after the call.
[12:50] Priya Patel: For the POC, we usually set up two tests: functional correctness (evals on your prompt set) and throughput/latency tests under your network path. We'll provide a benchmark harness you can run from a test instance.
[13:20] Jamal Reed: For the benchmark harness, do you want us to hit your PUBLIC endpoints or will we be talking to private endpoints?
[13:28] Priya Patel: For network realism we'll run from inside your VPC against the private endpoint or the deployed workers. We'll provide a small test cluster and a script \u2014 typical runs are 1k short requests and 100 long requests to measure p50/p95/p99.
[14:00] [16:45] Alex Morgan: Timeline \u2014 we want a POC in the next two weeks. Is that realistic?
[16:55] Marcus Chen: Yes, if we get approvals and your infra time. Key blockers are: security review signoff and network personnel time for creating endpoints and routes. If we get those greenlit, we can target a 2-week POC kickoff.
[17:20] Sara Lopez: We'll need the security pack before kickoff. Also we have a change freeze window next week, so ideal start is 10/19 but we could do prework earlier.
[17:35] Marcus Chen: Noted. We'll send the pack ASAP and can do prework (diagram review) before the freeze.
[18:00] [21:10] Lena Park: A question on model artifacts \u2014 do you pull models from our S3 or do you stage them to Redwood-managed storage? We want all artifacts in our account.
[21:25] Priya Patel: You can host artifacts in your S3. During deployment we pull from your S3 via an IAM role we assume in your account (only if you want). Otherwise, we can push to a customer-owned ECR/EFS. We also support immutable model versioning.
[21:50] Jamal Reed: IAM cross-account role is preferable. We'll lock down keys and tighten role permissions.
[22:05] Marcus Chen: Great. We'll include the exact IAM policy in the architecture doc.
[22:25] Priya Patel: Also note that for faster startup we can support model quantization and smaller footprints, which reduces EBS and memory footprint; we can recommend profiles based on your workload.
[22:50] [25:30] Alex Morgan: Cost question \u2014 what are the main levers? Latency vs cost tradeoffs?
[25:40] Marcus Chen: Biggest levers: instance type (GPU size), batching, KV/prefix caching hit rate, and quantization. Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) reduces variable cost and can improve latency consistency. We'll include cost projections in the proposal.
[26:10] Priya Patel: For POC we'll propose a small dedicated pool sized for your expected QPS for short prompts; we can provide run-rate vs reserved examples.
[26:35] [30:00] Sara Lopez: On legal/procurement, do you have standard DPA and security addendums?
[30:10] Marcus Chen: Yes \u2014 we have standard DPA, DSR handling, and can include additional contractual language for data residency. I'll loop in legal if needed.
[30:35] Priya Patel: Also worth noting, we can do a staged rollout: start with embeddings and summarize pipelines, then expand to generation if all good.
[31:00] Jamal Reed: For testing, we'll need a list of Redwood IPs and the endpoint DNS names.
[31:10] Marcus Chen: We'll provide an IP prefix list and private endpoint service name. Expect that in the architecture email.
[31:30] Lena Park: Any gotchas with AZ affinity? If workers are pinned to an AZ, do ENIs stay there?
[31:45] Priya Patel: ENIs are created per-subnet in the AZ. If you pin to AZs for locality you need to ensure sufficient subnet IPs and spread. We'll capture those requirements in a checklist.
[32:05] Alex Morgan: OK we're close on time. Quick recap?
[32:12] Marcus Chen: Recap: Redwood to send security pack + SOC2 artifacts, architecture diagram with both PrivateLink and in-VPC deployment options, IP prefixes and endpoint names, and pricing/proposal. Priya will schedule POC kickoff and share benchmark harness. Equinox runs network tests and compiles security questions. Target POC kickoff window 10/19-10/22 depending on change freeze.
[32:45] Sara Lopez: Sounds good. We'll prioritize the security review.
[33:00] Marcus Chen: Thanks everyone \u2014 any final questions?
[33:08] Alex Morgan: One small ask \u2014 can you include an example IAM policy snippet?
[33:15] Marcus Chen: Yes, we'll include an example assume-role policy and least-privilege docs.
[33:25] Priya Patel: I'll also attach the benchmark spreadsheet.
[33:35] [34:20] Jamal Reed: Alright thanks.
[34:25] Marcus Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the materials and next steps.
[34:40] [41:30] Call ends.

References/links mentioned: https://redwood.ai/docs/private-vpc (architecture diagram), security pack link (to be sent), benchmark spreadsheet (shared by Priya)
